kind: numerical-method bug fix (plan registration.amendment_rule): the bracket search of the photospheric density solve (photosphere.solve), used only where a state carries no photospheric density: the outer pressure of a seed, the predictor of the first relaxation step from a seed, and fold.classify of a state without one. Untouched: the photosphere row of the Newton system (photosphere.evaluate, which raises at Gamma_ph >= 1, so P_g <= 0 stays a model domain exit and is never clipped), the model surface (plan model.surface), every tolerance, the primary physics and microphysics, the targets and every immutable section.

The key enters the row-0 signature, so a row-0 model relaxed with the other bracket rule is never reused.

changes.section: photosphere.solve (no plan text: numerics of the implicit rho_ph that plan model.surface defines)
changes.registered: bracket 'doubling': from the guess (1e-12 g/cm3) the bracket is sought by doubling steps in ln rho_ph, and every trial density is evaluated with the domain check, so a trial with Gamma_ph >= 1 raises DomainError('Photospheric gas pressure is not positive (Gamma_ph >= 1); no Ball surface exists')
changes.amended: bracket 'scan': a trial with Gamma_ph >= 1 is an upper bound of the bracket (the row is continuous through Gamma_ph = 1: residual = P_g/scale - (1 - Gamma_ph), positive wherever Gamma_ph >= 1), and when the doubling scan finds no sign change the admissible interval (the microphysics domain reached from the guess, edges located by bisection) is scanned at 400 densities; 'Gamma_ph >= 1 at every admissible photospheric density' is raised only when that holds at every sampled density, otherwise 'not bracketed inside the microphysics domain'. A returned root is evaluated again with the domain check. Where the doubling scan brackets the root, the iterates and the root are those of 'doubling'.
changes.defect: kappa_ph, and with it Gamma_ph, depends on the trial density, so Gamma_ph >= 1 at one trial density says nothing about the root, which has P_g = target > 0, i.e. Gamma_ph < 1. The registered solve reports a missing photosphere where an ordinary root exists. On the MESA STARS opacity switch at 1e4 Msun: (2.195e8 Lsun, 3030 Rsun) and (3.48e8 Lsun, 3500 Rsun), roots at Gamma_ph 0.744 and 0.920; on a fixed 194-point (L, R) lattice (no table used) 41 of the 104 points with a root were reported as Gamma_ph >= 1, the 63 others solved identically by both rules, and the 90 true Gamma_ph >= 1 points are reported as such by both (first review, review_evidence/log_solve_grid.txt, brute force over 1500 densities). In the registered relaxation with Amendment 3 it makes the 3464 Rsun seed unbuildable at every N and rejects every first step of the 6000 Rsun seed at N = 400 at the predictor (review_evidence/log_oldsolve.txt; expected_relax_result_with_amendment_3_alone).

not_amended: The photosphere row of the step and of the frozen-entropy problem (photosphere.evaluate) and its domain check; the relaxation and its convergence and uniqueness criteria; the seed (Amendment 3); the relaxation mesh (Amendment 2). A guess outside the microphysics domain still raises its ValueError under either rule (a numerical failure, never a domain exit; no registered caller passes one: second review).

consequences_for_registered_runs: Order: Amendment 3 is registered and run alone first (its relax runs are this amendment's evidence); this amendment is then applied after it on every command: --amendment <3> --amendment <4> [...], the same flags in the same order on every later command.
With Amendments 3 and 4 the two seeds converge on different meshes and the relax runs end not_unique; those runs are the preserved failing runs Amendment 2 cites.
Every run directory records quasistatic.photosphere_bracket in config.yaml and this amendment's sha256 in amendments.json.
